title: Allow `covr::report()` to show coverage report even if a test failed
description:
If there is no technical obstacle, it would be nice to be able to still see the report even if the tests didn't pass.

Usecase: I'm testing a package with a large shiny app with `shinytest2` , so running the tests takes 10 minutes. I just ran `covr::report()` to see if I'm missing coverage on significant chunks, but because one test out of 1500 failed, the report didn't show. I need to fix a typo and wait another 10 minutes to see the coverage.

description:

title: Not reporting why covr failed due to substr lengths being bytes but used as character
description:
On  `show_failures()` sometimes `nchar(error_body, "bytes")` and `nchar(error_body)`, used by `substr()` are different which leads to empty strings after
https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/f1866d296c00884d1f085ff245669de01bc864c4/R/covr.R#L599  

See for example this situation:

```
Browse[1]> substr(error_body, body_len - (error_length - header_len), body_len)
[1] ""
Browse[1]> c(nchar(error_body), body_len - (error_length - header_len), body_len)
[1] 41092 41416 42276
Browse[1]> c(nchar(error_body, "bytes"), body_len - (error_length - header_len), body_len)
[1] 42276 41416 42276
```

One solution would be to measure string length in characters not bytes, another would be to just measure error length in "chars".

title: package_coverage() with code that loads the package via pkgload::load_all() re-instruments the namespace: coverage silently wiped to 0%, or a crash in exclude()
description:
### Summary

When the code passed to `package_coverage(code = )` loads the package under test through `pkgload::load_all()` — which is what `devtools::test()`, `testthat::test_local()` and `testthat::test_dir(load_package = "source")` all do — covr's injected `onLoad` hook fires a **second** time and runs `trace_environment()` on a namespace it has already instrumented. Two things then go wrong:

1. **Coverage data is silently destroyed.** `trace_environment()` begins with `clear_counters()`, so everything measured so far is discarded, and the second instrumentation pass produces counters with `srcref`s of eight `NA`s. Measured coverage drops to **0%** with no warning.
2. **In a package that uses `# nocov`, it is a hard error.** Those NA `srcref`s reach `exclude()`, which calls `seq(NA, NA)`:

```
Error in seq.default(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"]) :
  'from' must be a finite number
```

`per_line()` already guards exactly this hazard (`R/utils.R#152`, "In rare cases the source reference ... will not exists, so the first_line will be NA"); `exclude()` does not.

The crash is the visible symptom, but the loss of data is the primary defect: without `# nocov` the same run completes and reports 0%.

### Reproducer

Self-contained, no other package needed. Run verbatim:

```r
dir.create(pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "covrbug"))
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"))
writeLines(c(
  "Package: covrbug", "Title: Toy", "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Authors@R: person('A','B',email='a@b.c',role=c('aut','cre'))",
  "Description: Toy.", "License: MIT + file LICENSE", "Encoding: UTF-8"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
writeLines(c("YEAR: 2026", "COPYRIGHT HOLDER: A B"), file.path(pkg, "LICENSE"))
writeLines("export(g)", file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
writeLines(c(
  "g <- function(x) {",
  "  if (x > 0) y <- 'pos' else y <- 'neg'",
  "  y",
  "}",
  "# nocov start",
  "never_called <- function() message('unreachable')",
  "# nocov end"
), file.path(pkg, "R", "g.R"))

# A -- one instrumentation pass: fine
covr::package_coverage(pkg, type = "none", code = "invisible(covrbug::g(1))")
#> covrbug Coverage: 50.00%

# B -- a second trace_environment() on the same, already instrumented namespace
covr::package_coverage(pkg, type = "none", code = c(
  "invisible(covrbug::g(1))",
  "covr:::trace_environment(asNamespace('covrbug'))",
  "invisible(covrbug::g(-1))"))
#> Error in seq.default(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"]) :
#>   'from' must be a finite number

# C -- control: unload + reload is harmless (a clean namespace is re-instrumented)
covr::package_coverage(pkg, type = "none", code = c(
  "invisible(covrbug::g(1))", "unloadNamespace('covrbug')",
  "loadNamespace('covrbug')", "invisible(covrbug::g(-1))"))
#> covrbug Coverage: 50.00%
```

The explicit `covr:::trace_environment()` in B only stands in for what `load_all()` does. **No `:::` is needed to hit this.** With a `tests/testthat/` directory in the same toy package, only the `load_package` argument differs:

| `code =` | result |
|---|---|
| `testthat::test_dir(..., load_package = "installed")` | OK, 100% |
| `testthat::test_dir(..., load_package = "source")` | `'from' must be a finite number` |

So `covr::package_coverage(type = "none", code = 'devtools::test(filter = "...")')` — the natural way to scope a coverage run to a subset of tests — either crashes or silently reports 0%.

### Expected / actual

**Expected:** the coverage of the code that ran, or a clear error.

**Actual:**

| package | second pass | result |
|---|---|---|
| with `# nocov` | yes | error, `'from' must be a finite number` |
| without `# nocov` | yes | completes, reports **0%**, with NA-`srcref` counters manufactured |
| either | no | correct coverage |

Measured on the toy package above (identical command, only the second pass differs):

```
single pass : counters=4 NA-srcref=0 percent=50
double pass : counters=4 NA-srcref=1 percent=0
```

### Cause

The chain, all in covr 3.6.5:

1. `package_coverage()` installs the package and appends to the installed load script (`R/covr.R#792`, `add_hooks()`):

   ```r
   setHook(packageEvent(pkg, "onLoad"), function(...) covr:::trace_environment(ns))
   ```

   Instrumentation therefore happens in memory, at load time, in the test subprocess.

2. `pkgload::load_all()` loads the package again, so that user-level `onLoad` hook fires again.

3. `trace_environment()` (`R/covr.R#90-102`) starts with `clear_counters()` — every count accumulated so far is dropped — and then re-instruments an environment whose functions are **already** instrumented.

4. `replacement()` restores the original attributes onto the rewritten function, so the instrumented body still carries the srcrefs of the *original* source, which no longer line up with the (much larger) instrumented expression tree. On the second pass `trace_calls()` meets covr's own synthetic wrappers — `if (TRUE) { count(key); expr }` — which have no `srcref`, and falls back to `impute_srcref()` (`R/trace_calls.R#43`).

5. `impute_srcref()` indexes `pd_child` positionally: `make_srcref(3)`, `make_srcref(5)`, `make_srcref(7)` (`R/parse_data.R#57-59`). Against the mismatched tree those indices run past the end of `pd_child`. `make_srcref()` (`R/parse_data.R#33-50`) guards only `length(from) == 0`, not an out-of-range index, so `pd_child$line1[from]` yields `NA` and a `srcref` of eight `NA`s is built and registered.

6. `exclude()` (`R/exclusions.R#84-94`) then calls `seq()` on those rows and stops.

Full stack at the point of failure:

```
 6: covr::package_coverage(...)
 7: exclude(coverage, line_exclusions = line_exclusions, function_exclusions = ..., path = root)
 8: vlapply(seq_len(NROW(df)), function(i) { ... })
 9: vapply(X, FUN, ..., FUN.VALUE = logical(1))
10: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
11: seq(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"]) %in% excl[[file]]
12: seq(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"])
13: seq.default(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"])
14: stop("'from' must be a finite number")
```

The `# nocov` region is the second necessary condition for the crash: an NA-`srcref` counter only reaches the failing branch if its file carries line exclusions.

### Suggested patches

**1. Make `exclude()` NA-safe** (`R/exclusions.R#92`). This mirrors the guard `per_line()` already has, but as a predicate rather than a row drop — dropping rows from `df` here would misalign it with `coverage`, which `to_exclude` indexes positionally.

```diff
       !is.na(which_exclusion) &&
         (
           identical(excl[[which_exclusion]], Inf) ||
-          all(seq(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"]) %in% excl[[file]])
+          (is.finite(df[i, "first_line"]) &&
+           is.finite(df[i, "last_line"]) &&
+           all(seq(df[i, "first_line"], df[i, "last_line"]) %in% excl[[file]]))
         )
```

Applied to CRAN 3.6.5 and tested: run B stops erroring and returns a coverage object; the single-pass run is unchanged (50%); `# nocov` exclusion still works (`never_called` is still excluded). This also guards the `#576`/`#579` family of causes, which reached the same `seq()` from a different direction.

It does **not** fix the data loss — with the guard, run B returns `counters=4 NA-srcref=1 percent=0`. Hence:

**2. Make `trace_environment()` idempotent.** Re-instrumenting an already instrumented environment wipes the counters and manufactures NA `srcref`s. Either

* have `trace_environment()` return early when the environment it is handed is already traced (e.g. a marker set on the namespace, checked before `clear_counters()`), or
* have `make_srcref()` return `NULL` when the index misses, so covr degrades to "no srcref" instead of "eight NAs" — `impute_srcref()` already returns `NULL` on the neighbouring failure (`R/parse_data.R#16`).

The first addresses the cause; the second only prevents the crash. Happy to turn either into a PR if useful.

### Related, but not this

* **#576, #579** — same error message and the same `seq()` in `exclude()`, different cause: the R 4.4.0 `getParseData()` change. Closed by **#588**, which touched `NEWS.md`, `R/parse_data.R`, `R/utils.R` and `tests/testthat/test-utils.R` — `R/exclusions.R` was not modified, so the unguarded `seq()` is still there on `main` today.
* **#574** — `package_coverage()` failing when the package is already loaded. That is the *install* step refusing on Windows, fixed in 3.6.5; this report is about the *measurement* step, after a successful install.
* **#466** — 0% coverage caused by `skip_on_cran()` / `NOT_CRAN`. Different cause; the reproducer here has no tests at all.
* **#623** (open) — the same injected `onLoad` hook (`R/covr.R#792`), failing in a different way (cyclic namespace dependency).

### Session info

```
R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24 ucrt)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64
Running under: Windows 11 x64 (build 26200)

packages: covr 3.6.5, testthat 3.3.2, pkgload 1.5.3
```

Reproduced with `LANGUAGE=en`; source line numbers are from the CRAN 3.6.5 tarball
(`covr_3.6.5.tar.gz`, md5 `1414ace57aedd343a3992568538cc8ae`) and re-checked against
`main` (3.6.5.9001), where all four sites are unchanged.

title: Vulnerability with hard-coded old versions of bootstrap
description:
Some software blocks `covr` due to vulnerabilities in `bootstrap` (despite the fact that `bootstrap` may not be a true dependency of the main part of the package).  It looks like old versions of bootstrap are hard coded in a few places.  It seems changing these to version 3.4.1 would fix the issue with low risk (since it's the same major version), or switching to a much newer version could also work to remove the vulnerability, though functionality may have changed in the meantime.

In R/report.R, `bootstrap` 3.3.5 is hard coded:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/f1866d296c00884d1f085ff245669de01bc864c4/R/report.R#L281-L289

In tests/testthat/test-report.htm, `bootstrap` 3.3.7 is hard coded:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/f1866d296c00884d1f085ff245669de01bc864c4/tests/testthat/test-report.htm#L14-L17

It's here as well:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/f1866d296c00884d1f085ff245669de01bc864c4/inst/www/shared/bootstrap/css/bootstrap-theme.min.css#L2

It could be elsewhere.  Searching within GitHub isn't great.  For example, it doesn't show the last instance.

This may be the same issue as reported in #397, though I don't think the exact problem spots were pointed out there.

title: Running `covr` on already installed packages
description:
I'd like to be able to run `package_coverage` on a package, without needing to have the original package source folder downloaded locally.  That is, I want to be able to do:

```
remotes::install_github("kbodwin/mypackage", INSTALL_opts = "--install-tests")
covr::package_coverage(path.package("mypackage"))
```

While this process runs without error, it doesn't return any results.  I assume it's something to do with the installed version of the package, located at `path.package("mypackage")`, not having the exact folder structure of a true package source?

Or am I perhaps missing an argument to `package_coverage` that would make this work?


This might be a very niche use case; I'm wanting to auto-grade student-made packages.  I can't think of another reason to want to do this.  So, please feel free to deprioritize this request! :)

title: Automatic support for Coveralls on GItHub Actions
description:
This is a continuation of https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/457 with more clear objectives, now that we're debugged and understood exactly where the issues lie.

There is currently code (https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/caed186fc47884d1e848c09ddb9433716bd671c6/R/coveralls.R#L65-L70) that only adds git info to the coverage report if the CI is one of: [jenkins, drone, travis-pro]. This list needs to be also include "github-actions" (and the documentation should explicitly say that this string is supported).

This will get {covr} to attempt to attach git info, but it will not fully work yet. Specifically, the badge will not get updated because the branch will not be set correctly. This is because in https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/caed186fc47884d1e848c09ddb9433716bd671c6/R/coveralls.R#LL117C35-L117C58 it's looking for the envvar `CI_BRANCH` which does not exist in GitHub Actions. Perhaps using the `GITHUB_REF_NAME` envvar will work (I haven't tested it, but based on github actions' documentation it seems like it should).

Other than the branch not getting set correctly, the remote URL is also not set because it looks for a `CI_REMOTE` envvar, which again doesn't exist for github actions. Perhaps `system_output("git", c("config", "--get", "remote.origin.url"))` can be used for that.

And lastly, for code cleanliness purposes, it might be a good idea to rename the function `jenkins_git_info()` to just `get_it_info()`.

title: covr::coveralls() from github actions?
description:
I consistently get: 
```
 Error in covr::coveralls() : 
  Failed to upload coverage data. Reply by Coveralls: Couldn't find a repository matching this job.
```

Has anyone been able to get coveralls() working from github actions with this function? Possibly a way to pass parameters to make it work without any code modification? I've not been able to find any examples.

Scanning the code for `covr::coveralls()`, it appears that it is pretty specific to a travis-ci and possibly jenkins based CI environment. I'm having no luck getting it working and really like to maintain my history in coveralls if that's possible. 

It seems like there are two options -- 1) add github-actions logic to `covr::coveralls()` or 2) write a file that would be compatible with the [coveralls action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/coveralls-github-action). 

I think #442 is more or less calling for (2)? 

I'm not versed in LCOV -- how far is the output of this: from being an LCOV file? 
https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/master/R/coveralls.R#L43

title: `covr::to_sonarqube()` provides "path" attribute always with packagename
description:
Hi,

First of all: Thanks for this wonderful package! I enjoy it since I started with **R**.

I tried to use the already existing function `to_sonarqube()` to convert a test coverage and upload it to a sonarqube server.
In my case (and I think in most cases) the "root of the module" (see link below) is the package root.

In the current implementation (see tests/testthat/sonarqube.xml) the package name is always added:
```
path="TestSummary/R/TestSummary.R"
```

From my point of view the only way my sonarqube server is correctly interpreting the coverage report is:
```
path="R/TestSummary.R"
```
 
The [official documentation](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/test-coverage/generic-test-data#generic-test-coverage) provides the generic test coverage format.

My suggestions:

1) Remove packagename completely from path or
2) Provide an additional argument if the packagename should be included or not

I can provide an PR if a solution is found. The easiest way (and working with the most current versions of sonarqube) would be option 1. 

I hope we can discuss here what would be a proper approach!

Johannes

title: Feature request: Condition plus branch coverage
description:
## Preamble

Consider the following code and its corresponding test:

```r
empty <- function(df) {
  (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0 || ncol(df) == 0)
}

test_that("empty works", {
  expect_true(empty(NULL))
})
```

If you use `{covr}` to compute code coverage for a package that contains this function, it will be `100%`. 
But, note that the test covers only one of the conditions from the control statement (`is.null(df)`); the other two are untested and may contain bugs.

## FR

Is it possible for `{covr}` to also take into account all conditions—either on the same line or on different lines—while computing code coverage? 

With such an update, in the example above, the code coverage should be `0%` because the tests don't fully cover all the conditions on that line. I am not sure what should happen if the conditional statement spans multiple lines, but I can see how `0%` could be reasonable in that case as well. 

Related to, but still distinct from https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/279

description:

Backtrace:

title: `covr::package_coverage` does not register code run by `tinysnapshot` via `tinytest`
description:
`tinysnapshot` is a tinytest extension that can compare plotting outputs. To test functions that produce base plots, the user passes the plotting function to the exception function which then runs the plotting function and compares results with a standard.  (Demonstrated with pseudocode below.) Plotting functions run in this way are not being registered as covered. Full details and link to MRE in: https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/tinysnapshot/issues/29

I'm unsure whether this is a bug in covr, tinytest, or tinysnapshot. In any case, input from covr maintainers on the issue and possible solutions would be very welcome!



# Simplified tinysnapshot flow

**tinysnapshot**
```r
expect_snapshot_plot <- function(plotting_fn, id) {
  # setup
  ....
  # run function
  plotting_fn()
  # compare results
  ...
}
```

**in package under test**
```r
my_custom_plotting_function <- function(){
  ...
  plot(...)
  ...
}
```

**test file in package under test**
```r
expect_snapshot_plot(my_custom_plotting_function, 'test_my_custom_plotting_function')
```

title: A code coverage badge without codecov.io
description:
The covr package is doing all the heavy lifting of computing code coverage for R packages but the very last step: the badge creation for display on the README, relies on a third-party service.

This:

- reduces interoperability with different hosting platforms (as described in [@adamhsparks' blog post](https://adamhsparks.netlify.app/2026/01/24/look-ma-no-codecov-io/) for Codeberg).
- adds an extra layer of required maintenance. This was well illustrated when codecov.io started requiring PATs and most workflows started failing (https://github.com/r-lib/actions/commit/dac574fb90b66a5abc1d4c2b1df1578085428a34).
- generally adds a dependency on a 3rd-party service which could start degrading or monetizing its offer at any point in time.

But all this could easily be avoided by offering the creation of the badge locally in covr, without the upload to codecov.io. It seems a relatively low lift compared to the work covr is already doing.

I would be happy to submit a PR if you agree this would be a valuable feature.

Related blog posts:
- https://adamhsparks.netlify.app/2026/01/24/look-ma-no-codecov-io/
- (for completeness, but more related to the other feature codecov.io is offering. Would be required for an entire decoupling from codecov.io: https://jakubsobolewski.substack.com/p/want-to-get-code-coverage-report)

cc @maelle @adamhsparks.

title: Documentation: Should covr users declare it in their Suggests?
description:
Most users of `covr` do so in their package CI, not actually using `covr` exports in their package code directly.

By CRAN rules then, there's no need to declare a dependency on `covr`, but I imagine it would still help the `covr` maintainers see at a glance who's using the package if the users declared so in Suggests.

OTOH, GitHub search will probably yield most of the same results by identifying repos calling `covr::codecov()`.

Is there any official guidance from `covr` on the maintainers' preferences here?

title: Coverage of implicit 'else' branch
`covr::package_coverage` fails to find any tests

title: Rare edge cases in `count_test` and `clean_coverage_tests`
description:
Hi!

In our enterprise solution, we have discovered a peculiar edge case when `count_test` function is called with `.current_test` not yet initialized, leading to error:

```
Error in tests$.data[[1L]] <- .current_test$index : 
  replacement has length zero
```

For us, we encountered it when calculating coverage for the  `digest` when using `tinytest` Ubuntu libraries (funnily enough, when installing tinytest from source, the issue did not appear). That makes reproducing the issue really tedious, although I was able to do it on macOS as well. Nevertheless, I believe the most straightforward approach is to add an if statement to cover that edge case, even if it's super rare, simply to make sure the `covr` is not vulnerable to weird/unexpected package combinations in the future.

Similarly, we've experienced another rare edge case when testing the full `renv` testing suite:

```
```
Error in `if (is.null(n <- nrow(obj[[i]]$tests$tally)) || n <
   val) next`:
   ! missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

As in the previous case, I believe that making sure that the value there is always logical does not harm the package, but ensures its stability even in weird edge cases.

title: Error with `x |> switch(case = , fallthrough = )` pattern.
description:
Hi!

I see a covr failure when code uses the `switch()` fallthrough idiom (`case = ,`) and the base pipe `|>`.

Below is an MRE reprex demonstrating. Running coverage fails during covr’s instrumented test with: `argument is missing, with no default`

``` r
pkg <- fs::path(tempfile(), "covrswitch")
fs::dir_create(pkg)

oldwd <- setwd(pkg)

fs::dir_create("R")
fs::dir_create("tests/testthat")

title: Running covr for httr/R6 lead to cyclic namespace dependency failure
description:
Hi!

Recently, while working on the validated package repository, we discovered that it is no longer possible to calculate coverage for R6 and httr packages, as the calculation returns NaN coverage and an error message.

```
> library('httr')
Error in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]) : 
  cyclic namespace dependency detected when loading 'httr', already loading 'covr', 'httr'
```

We have investigated the issue, only for `httr` and `R6`, but it will, in fact, affect any package that `covr` imports via NAMESPACE and was introduced in https://github.com/r-lib/covr/commit/1dbc608baf3fea18b981d3f9c4c4a1622e5ff178 by importingFrom `httr` package, which inherently, importsFrom `R6`.

```
library(covr)
sessionInfo()
(...)
other attached packages:
[1] covr_3.6.4.9007

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] httr_1.4.7     compiler_4.5.0 lazyeval_0.2.2 R6_2.6.1       rex_1.2.1      tools_4.5.0   
```

`rex`, on the other hand, which is loaded because it is used in .onLoad, does not result in a cyclic namespace because it is not, in fact, imported via it.

More specifically, the cyclic dependency is caused by hooks added to the package:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/5609fb8baaee6dd74c0bcca2f1ab43f6ce49cf73/R/covr.R#L792

Upon loading R6 (let's use this package as an example for simplicity), the triple colon operator in `covr:::trace_environment` tries to load `covr` NAMESPACE, which loads `httr`, which loads `R6`, resulting in a loop.

I'd like to ask whether it is something you would consider implementing/accepting a fix for. Right now, it affects only two packages, but it makes it possible that in the future, even more packages will be excluded from calculating coverage.

If you decide to fix it and the fix isn't to remove these imports, I was doing some experiments with custom code coverage calculation that might be useful.  If we skip attaching the package and proceed directly to custom code in:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/5609fb8baaee6dd74c0bcca2f1ab43f6ce49cf73/R/covr.R#L757-L759

We could first attach `covr` from the main library (and deps), then force detach of the package that we want calculated coverage of (like R6) and reload it from the `covr` custom library with hooks attached. Then we don't enter the loop as the `covr` would already be loaded.

Let me know what you think about this problem. I can help with implementing/further elaboration if you think it's worth pursuing.

title: line coverage value mismatch between print()/tally_coverage() and report()
description: With my package I have an example where the coverage given by print() is different from the one give by report(). I did not manage to create a reproducible example, but I think the problem lies in a different implementation between the two methods. The code in question is in that function: Using report() or package_coverage(), line 177 appears covered. But using print() or tally_coverage(), I get: ``` tally_coverage(x) 90 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 183 16 842 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 176 16 843 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 177 0 844 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 178 16 845 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 179 16 846 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 180 2 847 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 181 16 848 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 183 16 print(x) > x srcpkgs Coverage: 99.88% R/pkg_test.R: 98.89% [...] as.data.frame(x) > 60 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 176 3 178 3 3 3 1052 1054 16 61 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 177 9 177 21 9 21 1053 1053 196 62 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 177 24 177 29 24 29 1053 1053 0 63 R/pkg_test.R summary.pkg_test 177 36 177 41 36 41 1053 1053 196 > covr:::per_line(x)[["R/pkg_test.R"]]$coverage[177] [1] 196 ``` As you can see, for `tally_coverage(x)`, line 177 has 0 coverage, while for report() and per_line(), it has 196 coverage. I guess this is caused by line `if (is.logical(x)) any(x) else sum(x) `, for which its 2 clauses are in the same line, and one is actually tested but not the other. Still it seems that there are two different ways of computing the coverage, and probably the correct way is the most conservative, as computed by `tally_coverage(x)`

title: snapshot testing and coverage metric
description:
hi, I have found that when we have multiple snapshot testing within one unit test, like here:
```
test_that("test 1", {
  # some code
  expect_snapshot_file()

  # some other code
  expect_snapshot_file()
})
```

the lines executed in the second snapshot testing appear as not covered. If I take that chunk out and put it as a separate unit test, then magically the overall coverage increases:
```
test_that("test 1", {
  # some code
  expect_snapshot_file()
})

test_that("test 2", {
  # some other code
  expect_snapshot_file()
})
```
Is this the expected behaviour? Did anyone else see a similar pattern?

Thank you.

title: Consider using '-a' to get within-line coverage data
description:
As intimated in https://github.com/r-lib/covr/pull/608#issuecomment-2870196454, this looks like a pretty platform-robust way to get sub-line granularity of coverage (hence related to #604):

https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Invoking-Gcov.html#Invoking-gcov

> Write individual execution counts for every basic block. Normally gcov outputs execution counts only for the main blocks of a line. With this option you can determine if blocks within a single line are not being executed.

I'm not sure if this is complementary or at odds with #609, if at odds, #609 should still be preferred where possible since having structured data as the output will always be preferred to a text output we need to process manually.

title: Strict mode for requiring full line coverage (in gcov)?
description:
For some years, we've slowly been adding newlines to code to improve our code coverage due to {covr} reporting full coverage of partially-covered lines, e.g.

```diff
-if (verbose) Rprintf("reached.\n");
+if (verbose)
+  Rprintf("reached.\n");
```

Now I am learning a bit more about `gcov` internals:

https://github.com/Rdatatable/data.table/issues/6950#issuecomment-2863266519

It seems `gcov` indeed recognizes this line is only partially covered if the test suite always uses `verbose=0` by reporting `1*` "partially covered":

https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Invoking-Gcov.html

Can this somehow be reported to the user? Is there any option to require lines be fully-covered in order for codecov to consider them "covered" in a 0/1 sense?

title: Use --json-format for gcov reports to get pre-structured results
description:

https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Invoking-Gcov.html

And thankfully we already import {jsonlite}:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/d8d33b41b6b013a3e96ea04cb6d1bf434c4822d2/DESCRIPTION#L51

---

Currently, `gcov` output is parsed with regular expressions:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/d8d33b41b6b013a3e96ea04cb6d1bf434c4822d2/R/compiled.R#L18-L37

I think it will be much more robust and extensible to use the structured JSON output instead.

title: segfault when using a `fastmap` to store data read using `arrow`
description:
I've been trying to chase down this bug for a while, and although I don't have a solution I've tried my best to pin down a reproducible example in a reprex over in [dgkf/reprex-covr-segfault](https://github.com/dgkf/reprex-covr-segfault).

In short, a package that uses a pattern such as

```r
function(f) {
  m <- fastmap::fastmap()  
  m$set("data", arrow::read_parquet(f))
}
```

will segfault when trying to calculate code coverage. 

At it's core, it _usually_ segfaults any time a package tries to store a `arrow` `data.frame` inside a `fastmap` stored somewhere within the package namespace.

I say _usually_ because coverage will run to completion on the current CRAN release of `covr` if there is an `if`  statement (and maybe others?) somewhere in the package code. I was only able to reliably test this by putting an `if (TRUE) {}` statement in the `.onLoad` function, but the behavior was rather sporadic and I think it's also affected by the presence/absence of S3 method registration. The development version of CRAN fails regardless.

title: `install_path` parameter breaks in WINDOWS subprocesses
description:
When running the `covr` in the `callr` subprocess on Windows, `covr::package_coverage` unexpectedly breaks if `install_path` has double backslashes (valid WINDOWS path) `\\` instead of the single forward slashes `/`. That's due to the path normalization which happens after creating the directory: 

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/ca4241da03a30b76a8d8cbfc194371cb94ca512e/R/covr.R#L413-L415

Swapping these two lines will make the internal `normalize_path` function first replace all the `\\` with `/` so the function can proceed as expected. I'm not sure why exactly this is an issue in a subprocess, but the change looks reasonable either way.

title: add a markdown output function
description:
an exported function like `cover::markdown_output()` to print a coverage report in markdown, which could then easily be used to add either a [Job Summary](https://github.blog/2022-05-09-supercharging-github-actions-with-job-summaries/) for a GH Action, or potentially to add a comment to a PR thread with a coverage report. I played around making a more sophisticated `markdown()` function than what @jimhester suggested [here](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/207#issuecomment-233380177). In my GH Action, I ran a coverage test on both HEAD and on MAIN and generated a markdown coverage report comparing the diff. (This is quick and dirty, but maybe of interest for ideas.) ``` yaml - name: test-coverage id: coverage run: | markdown_cov_diff <- function(head, main) { group <- "filename" by = "line" sig_num <- 2 tally_head <- covr::tally_coverage(head, by = by) tally_main <- covr::tally_coverage(main, by = by) percs_head <- tapply(tally_head$value, tally_head[[group]], FUN = function(x) sum(x > 0) / length(x) * 100) percs_main <- tapply(tally_main$value, tally_main[[group]], FUN = function(x) sum(x > 0) / length(x) * 100) percs_diff <- unname(percs_head - percs_main) ttl_perc_head <- covr::percent_coverage(tally_head, by = by) ttl_perc_main <- covr::percent_coverage(tally_main, by = by) ttl_perc_diff <- ttl_perc_head - ttl_perc_main percs_head <- format(percs_head, digits = sig_num) percs_main <- format(percs_main, digits = sig_num) percs_diff <- paste0(ifelse(percs_diff < 0, ":small_red_triangle_down: ", ""), ifelse(percs_diff > 0, ":arrow_up: ", ""), format(percs_diff, digits = sig_num)) ttl_perc_head <- format(ttl_perc_head, digits = sig_num) ttl_perc_main <- format(ttl_perc_main, digits = sig_num) ttl_perc_diff <- paste0(ifelse(ttl_perc_diff < 0, ":small_red_triangle_down: ", ""), ifelse(ttl_perc_diff > 0, ":arrow_up: ", ""), format(ttl_perc_diff, digits = sig_num)) paste0( "
\n", "Coverage Report\n\n", "|file|head|main|diff|\n|", " :-- | --: | --: | --: |\n", paste0("|Overall|", ttl_perc_head, "%|", ttl_perc_main, "%|", ttl_perc_diff, "%|", "\n"), paste0("|", names(percs_head), "|", percs_head, "%|", percs_main, "%|", percs_diff, "%|", collapse = "\n"), "\n", "
" ) } head <- covr::package_coverage() system2("git", c("checkout", "main")) main <- covr::package_coverage() writeLines(markdown_cov_diff(head, main), "coverage-report.md") shell: Rscript {0} ``` I've experimented with this a bit, and I have been successful with both. job summary looked like this: ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1708872/203757657-a03344bf-fc4f-4dc5-a0e0-f1cbeec55ac6.png) PR thread comment looks like: example markdown table for a PR thread comment: ``` markdown
Coverage Report |file|head|diff| | :-- | --: | --: | |Overall|57%|:small_red_triangle_down: -0.074%| |R/function_one.R|91%|0.0%| |R/function_two.R|71%|:arrow_up: 0.0%| |R/function_three.R|94%|:small_red_triangle_down: -1.1%|
``` renders as:
Coverage Report |file|head|diff| | :-- | --: | --: | |Overall|57%|:small_red_triangle_down: -0.074%| |R/function_one.R|91%|0.0%| |R/function_two.R|71%|:arrow_up: 0.0%| |R/function_three.R|94%|:small_red_triangle_down: -1.1%|

title: bug: `covr::codecov()` should throw an error if unable to upload coverage results to codecov.io
description:
### Description

`covr::codecov()` should throw an error if unable to upload coverage results to codecov.io

### Actual Behaviour

If `covr::codecov()`  fails to upload coverage results to codecov.io it does not throw an error, the corresponding github action is thus marked as successful in github.

The devs are not notify that there was a failure in the workflow.

See this [workflow](https://github.com/ALanguillaume/test.cd.pkgdown.gh/actions/runs/8631978564/job/23662656061)

![image](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/assets/43757522/791f2adf-bf6a-4339-8778-d163702eeabd)


### Expected Behaviour

`covr::codecov()` throws an error if unable to upload coverage results to codecov.io.
-> gh action workflow fails
-> devs are notified

### Additional context

Related to https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/822

title: package_coverage() can fail if the package is already loaded
description:
On Windows, R will refuse to install a package if that package is already loaded, even if the package is being installed into some independent library paths. This error comes from here:

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/0b3e527dc50303c6e320deb7bb2d11a02d636b71/src/library/utils/R/packages2.R#L278-L295

And `install.packages()` gets invoked here:

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/dd5286dd7cb3909456637a52d942f2428fa0a926/R/covr.R#L443-L455

This implies that a workflow like:

```
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test_coverage()
```

will fail, as the package we want to run coverage on is already loaded.

title: [covr.record_tests] segfault when tracing R6 active bindings to parquet data
description:
> [!NOTE]  
> This is in code I introduced and only affects very specific scenarios when `options(covr.record_tests)` is enabled.  
> **I plan to fix this**

### Example at [dgkf/covr-r6-active-binding-test](https://github.com/dgkf/covr-r6-active-binding-test)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/dgkf/covr-r6-active-binding-test
cd covr-r6-active-binding-test
R -e 'options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)' -e 'covr::package_coverage()'
```

### Details

From what I can tell, there are a few key features of this package that culminate in this bug:

- An R6 active binding is included in the test call stack
  - For reasons that are still unclear to me, the [`sys.calls()` captured in `update_current_test()`](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/main/R/trace_tests.R#L189), when capturing an active binding, includes the R _function_, not just the _call_. Critically, this function brings its calling environment.
- When the R6 object environment includes a parquet dataset (I'm assuming due to the way arrow works with the in-memory representation of the data), this environment segfaults when serialized to disk.

### Proposed solution

- Will first try to drill into why this is grabbing a function. There might be a more holistic way to avoiding this altogether.
- If there's no better way to avoid functions in the call stack, then before recording the call stack, if a frame contains a function, set its environment to `emptyenv()` so it can be serialized.

title: `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`: tests being captured multiple times in for loops
description:
In light of #527, I wanted to let you know that we've discovered a behavior in the last couple days related to the `options(cov.record_tests = TRUE)` that I'd like to fix. If we can squeeze a fix into this release that would be awesome.

The overall behavior isn't _wrong_, but can result in really big coverage objects with inflated `attr(<coverage obj>, "tests")` due to how we currently decide when to log a new test. In most cases, the bloat is negligible, but the [`fastmap` package](https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap) piqued our interest because it is a rather pathological case where the bloat increases the object size by a few orders of magnitude. This is enough to crash the containers we're running the evaluation in. 

I've already pinpointed what needs to change, but it will take me a day or so to make the fix. There is a simple case that is just a couple lines of code change, and a non-trivial case that would require a bit more machinery to avoid duplicate test records.

# What's causing the bloat?

## The simple case

When the same test is hit repeatedly in a loop, we are currently recording a "new" test for each call from the test code.

The issue lies in the heuristics we use to determine when we're onto a new test call. When tests are evaluated in a loop (for example, [this `for` loop from `fastmap`](https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap/blob/147830b6e691cc5f2da44f6c956f5164e122d75a/tests/testthat/test-map.R#L274-L292)), we record a new test each time the evaluation frame changes. Instead, we should only consider it as a new test if the _calling_ frame changes. This is a simple fix, and just means we need to take the `parent.env()` instead of the `sys.frame` itself.

Fixing this is just a matter of changing a couple lines, and [is already implemented](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/commit/67d511aeabb9ac3c17f9569a5a6e3b328746c868).

## The non-trivial case

This is a bit more complicated when we _alternate_ calls into a package within a loop (as seen in [this `for` loop from `fastmap`](https://github.com/r-lib/fastmap/blob/147830b6e691cc5f2da44f6c956f5164e122d75a/tests/testthat/test-queue.R#L243-L256), alternating between `q$remove` and `q$add`). In this case the call is changing and our heuristic is working as intended, but because we only check to see if the _last_ test is the same, each alternating call is still recorded.

To address this, I'd like to build a vector of test hashes (probably just a srcref string, ie `file:line:col`) of test calls that we can reference to see if the current test has already been logged and add a new column to each trace's test log that includes a record of how many times each test call was called. Proposed change to documented structure would look like

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/caed186fc47884d1e848c09ddb9433716bd671c6/R/trace_tests.R#L80-L83
```diff
  #' # $`source.Ref2326138c55:3:8:3:8:8:8:3:3`
- #' #      test depth i
- #' # [1,]    1     1 1
- #' # [2,]    1     2 3
+ #' #      test call depth i
+ #' # [1,]    1    1     1 1
+ #' # [2,]    2    1     1 1
+ #' # [3,]    1    2     2 3
+ #' # [4,]    2    2     2 3
```
 
 [I implemented this today](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/commit/aa538fcf4773d1b9b34e1de2e7a00f053b733699), but the code isn't to a level of quality that I'm happy with yet and I want to do a little refactoring still before contributing it.

title: Coverage with modules (e.g. klmr/box)
description:
### Background
We use [klmr/box](https://github.com/klmr/box) (previously we used [wahani/modules](https://github.com/wahani/modules)) to structure the code of our Shiny apps. These packages bring a module/import system similar to what you can find in languages like Python, JavaScript (ES6+) or Java.

Each module has its own namespace and multiple modules can export objects with identical names. For example, we can have modules named `main.R` and `sidebar.R` both of which export `ui` and `server` objects. When using them in some other module, they can be referred to e.g. as `main$server` and `sidebar$server`. This also works in our testthat unit tests - the test file itself imports the functions it needs to test.

Unfortunately the covr package is not prepared for this kind of usage. The `file_coverage()` function just sources all files passed in the `source_files` argument, so any duplicate names in the modules clash and overwrite each other. The generated coverage report has files missing.

### Goal
We'd love to use covr to generate coverage report for our Shiny apps, but we find modules very important for structuring large apps, and these two tools are currently incompatible. I'd like to start a discussion - how can we change that?

I'm happy to provide more details, e.g. prepare a demo project.

title: [Feature Request] Add support for longtests in `package_coverage()`
description:
## Description
This feature would allow users to specify a new parameter, `type = "longtests"`, in the `package_coverage()` function. This would be useful for Bioconductor users who want to divide their tests into two folders, one for normal tests and one for long tests that take longer to run.

## Context
Currently, Bioconductor software packages run code in the `tests` subdirectory on a daily basis as part of the Bioconductor nightly builds. The maximum amount of time that `R CMD check` is allowed to spend on each package is 40 minutes. However, some package developers may wish to implement tests that will be too long to run in the context of the nightly builds. To address this issue, Bioconductor users can set up “long tests” in their package and add the package to the Bioconductor Long Tests builds. The code in the `longtests` subdirectory will be run once a week (every Saturday) as part of the Long Tests builds and will be allowed to run for a maximum of 6 hours before a TIMEOUT is raised.

## Justification
Adding support for the `type = "longtests"` parameter in the `package_coverage()` function would allow Bioconductor users to generate coverage reports for their long tests separately from their normal tests. This would make it easier for users to identify which tests are taking longer to run and optimize their testing process accordingly.

## Implementation details
The `type = "longtests"` parameter would be added to the `package_coverage()` function. The `longtests` folder would have the same structure as the `tests` folder, but with a different name.

## Example usage
```
covr::package_coverage(type = "longtests")
```

title: Test coverage for a single file
description:
`devtools::test_coverage_active_file()` is proving increasingly useful in our workflow where there's (in most cases) there's a one-to-one relationship between files in `R/` and in `tests/testthat/`. However, because covr `environment_coverage()` calls `sys.source()` rather than `testthat::test_file()` we have to recreate much of the `test_file()` infrastructure in `test_coverage_active_file()`. And that's fragile and continues to cause problems (see https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/pull/2537 for a recent example).

Could we have a variant of `environment_coverage()` (either a new argument or a new function) that'd call `testthat::test_file()`?

Or maybe something like this?

```R
with_coverage <- function(code,
                          env = parent.frame(),
                          line_exclusions = NULL,
                          function_exclusions = NULL) {
  exec_env <- new.env(parent = env)
  trace_environment(env)
  on.exit({
    reset_traces()
    clear_counters()
  })
  withr::with_envvar(c(R_COVR = "true"), code)

  coverage <- as_coverage(.counters)
  exclude(
    coverage,
    line_exclusions = line_exclusions,
    function_exclusions = function_exclusions,
    path = NULL
  )
}
```

title: Coverage for tests
description:
It would be useful to report coverage for files under `tests`:

 1. The `tests` directory may contain code that is not a test itself but it is supposed to be used by tests. If that code is not used, it can probably be removed.
 2. Knowing which `tests` are actually run (and if a test stopped running for some reason) is useful.
 3. `pytest --covr` does report coverage for tests, which allows setting different codecov components/flags with different status criteria for `R` and `tests`. (For example, we may require that coverage for tests cannot decrease of the CI fails)
 
The option [`covr.record_tests`](https://covr.r-lib.org/reference/covr.record_tests.html) does a lot more than just recording coverage for tests.

#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpT9LnNK/typetracer//src/utils.gcno"

description:

Pedro

title: codecov.io security breach
description:
It appears that codecov had a serious security breach related to Bash Uploader, see https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=26819983 (their website is currently down, so linking Hacker News instead). As many users just revived a securit notice, it would be helpful to narrow down which projects are affected.

At a first glance it seems that r-lib/covr does not download the bash uploader, so it should NOT be affected, but some users might have possibly received a notification as there seems to be a shared use of API/code that might have lead to false positives: 

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/c6d10d9b6ffec0521e49eb5388f5e3a6d47e4bd7/R/codecov.R#L161-L184

- Could you please confirm that users of covr were not affected?
- Could you please set-up security policy/advisories (https://github.com/r-lib/covr/security) for future?

Many thanks for your great work!

title: "covr" and R6 classes
description:
I have an R package with several R6 classes. Some of the function names of these classes are identical (e.g., initialize  
R6 class A has an initialize method, and class B has an initialize method).
That means a function name is used multiple times in an R package.
The test coverage for these functions is reported together if both classes are declared in the same R file.
I understand that one option to address the issue is to declare each R6 class in a separate file, then run coverage and afterward group the results by "filename" and "functions" to obtain the coverage for a specific R6 class function.

Or is there a different way to implement 'covr' support for R6?

title: Cobertura coverage-04.dtd validation?
description:
While trying to use the coverage report generated by `to_cobertura` in VS Code for nicely color-coded [coverage gutters](https://github.com/ryanluker/vscode-coverage-gutters), I have found the following issues with the XML currently being generated:

- The `<method>` nodes are currently generated without a `complexity` attribute, which [may or may not be required](https://github.com/cobertura/cobertura/issues/425). Should I add a `complexity="0"` attribute just for safety's sake? This would entail being explicit about the DTD we claim to adhere to.
- The parser which the above mentioned Coverage Gutters project uses [expects](https://github.com/fschwaiger/cobertura-parse/blob/82b0333cb1580f6f337b5d44b04e2f5ca8711b7e/source/index.js#L75) a filled `<sources>` node as child of the `<coverage>` node. Neither of the two DTDs actually expects at least one child, but I think adding the current working directory would not hurt.

@jimhester has touched the relevant `R/cobertura.R` before; good if I base a PR off of this issue?

title: covr with `option(covr.record_tests = TRUE)` segfaults with large tests
description:
Posting this primarily for myself since it's an issue related to code I contributed (or rather [with R itself](https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18348)) and plan to add some guardrails to prevent. It's extremely rare, but very opaque when it occurs. 

### Overview

When `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`, the call stack of each unique test is recorded alongside the trace hits. These are written out with the `.counters` environments to `.Rds` files and read back in to aggregate coverage. However, R's `.Rds` deserializer can segfault when a call has an enormous number of arguments (documented in [this comment in the R source](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/52b730f217c12ba3d95dee0cd1f330d1977b5ea3/src/main/serialize.c#L105-L117) referenced in [my Rlang bug report](https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18348)). 

### Specific Example

This was encountered while running `covr` against the `fs` package with `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`, which has [one test that checks against super long file paths by calling the `fs::path` function with 100K arguments](https://github.com/r-lib/fs/blob/e7d98c4c6abb15d885804c622317e6ee313a1524/tests/testthat/test-path.R#L55). R will segfault when trying to deserialize this call from `.Rds` when reading back in the `.counters` object.

### Proposed Fix

This is an exceedingly rare circumstance, but one that produces rather indecipherable crash. To avoid this scenario, I propose truncating calls that exceed some conservative limit (say, 10K arguments, which is safely below the 25K minimum to produce the crash on my system). 

A small pre-processing step would be needed before [this line](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/22ff6ae236c20810c1434caec3d31936147921f4/R/trace_tests.R#L187), for example:

```r
max_call_len <- 1e4 + 1
call_lengths <- vapply(test, length, numeric(1L))
if (any(call_lengths > max_call_len)) {
  warning("A large call was captured as part of a test and will be truncated.")
}

test <- lapply(test, head, max_call_len)
```

Even if this behavior is resolved in a future version of R, it would be nice to conditionally make this truncation for older versions of R where this would still be problematic.

title: covr with `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)` causes error when `.libPaths()` are modified mid-test-suite
description:
Posting this primarily as a TODO item for myself, as this is related to code that I contributed. 

### Overview

Discovered when running `covr::package_coverage` with `options(covr.record_tests)` against package `renv`, it seems that accessing `.libPaths()` within the `renv` test is causing an error. This hasn't been a problem in the past, but operating on the assumption that library paths are not mutated throughout testing is perhaps too assumptive and may require broader revision to the way that test srcrefs are identified.

```
Error in `normalizePath(.libPaths()[[1]])`:
(converted from warning) path[1]="/tmp/Rtmpku41Ov/renv-test-83bf4993f94c/renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu": 
  No such file or directory 

Backtrace: 
1. renv:::test_that(...) at test-infrastructure.R:31:0 
2. renv:::stopf("test %s has corrupted libpaths", shQuote(desc)) at tests/testthat/helper-aaa.R:51:4 
3. covr:::count("utils-format.R:13:3:13:40:3:40:28278:28278") 
4. covr:::count_test(key) 
5. covr:::update_current_test(key) 
6. base::startsWith(syscall_srcfile[has_srcfile], normalizePath(.libPaths()[[1]]))
```

### Proposed fix

As a first pass at this, the immediate error would be resolved by removing assumption that `.libPaths()` always has length >= 1 and add error handling when using `normalizePath` (I think `mustWork = FALSE` will be sufficient). 

In the longer term, it might be necessary to capture the testing lib that covr kicks off the testing with instead of using `.libPaths()` as it exists throughout the testing execution. This would be a bit more involved, and I'm not sure off hand what would be the best way to propagate this library path to each `count` trace call. Possibilities include:
  - Passing the path to each trace call (not ideal as it would affect trace injection in a way that is unnecessary when `covr.record_tests = FALSE` - ie most cases)
  - Using an internal stateful environment similar to the `.counters` environment to log the package test installation library for reference when discovering test trace srcrefs. This is less invasive, but relies on more state being managed by the `covr` namespace.

title: codecov Fails during Travis with error [unsafe repository]
description:
Hello, 

Couples days ago, our build stops working suddenly in Travis with the following error message.
```
* DONE (csa.r)
Running specific tests for package ‘csa.r’
  Running ‘testthat.R’
fatal: unsafe repository ('/mnt/app' is owned by someone else)
To add an exception for this directory, call:
	git config --global --add safe.directory /mnt/app
Error in system(full, intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = quiet, ...) : 
  running command ''git' 'rev-parse' '--abbrev-ref' 'HEAD'' had status 128
Calls: <Anonymous> ... withCallingHandlers -> <Anonymous> -> force -> system
Execution halted
```
Our travis is built using docker container. Within travis, we ran a shell script that execute the following for Codecov.
```
R_PCT_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD <- 63

# create covr coverage_object
coverage_obj <-
  covr::package_coverage(quiet = FALSE,
                         clean = FALSE,
                         type = "tests"
  )

 # upload results to codecov
 covr::codecov(coverage = coverage_obj,
               token = Sys.getenv('CODECOV_TOKEN'))


# calculate package coverage
total_coverage <- covr::percent_coverage(coverage_obj)
total_coverage <- round(total_coverage, digits = 2)
message(paste0("Total coverage is ", total_coverage))

if (total_coverage < R_PCT_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD) {
  message(paste0("Total coverage is less than ", R_PCT_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD))
  # quit with non-zero exit code
  quit(save = "no", status = 1)
}
```

Apparently, the error was caused by  `covr::codecov(coverage = coverage_obj, token = Sys.getenv('CODECOV_TOKEN'))`.
After commenting that line out, everything works. 

Is there a way to address this error rather than commenting it out?

title: Add an option to report source-root-relative paths
description:
`covr::package_coverage()` uses paths relative to the root of the R package by default, or absolute paths with `relative = FALSE` . None of these options is great for repositories where the R package sits underneath some subdirectory (duckdb, arrow, igraph, ...) . The problem occurs when trying to upload these coverage reports to codecov or other services. See e.g. https://codecov.io/gh/duckdb/duckdb/compare/624fa8aa4d81f812d7dc8d83620f914a76b3b114...e675b3dce58b120ca87574736f4c2386c1ddbcce/changes: this PR adds coverage checks for the R package that lives in `tools/rpkg` (via `covr::codecov("tools/rpkg")` but the files are not referred to by their relative root. This causes confusion with the other coverage checks in the project.

I propose supporting a third option, e.g. `relative = "wd"` or perhaps `relative = getwd()` where all paths would be stored relative to the working directory. Fixing this here is way easier than working around at the user level, it is very cumbersome to tweak the data structure returned by `covr::package_coverage()` .

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: Output of `file_coverage()` does not contain attribute `package$path`
description:
Thanks for this package.

Since a short while ago, we use `tinytest` for unit testing, since it is dependency-free. The `tinytest` package requires users to add their tests to `inst/tinytest`, which is not picked up by `covr:package_coverage()`. Whether `tinytest` should be supported by `covr` is another issue, I'm here now for your implementation of manual supporting other ways of picking up unit tests. 

So as a workaround we now use `covr::file_coverage()`, but it does not contain a `path` argument and nor does it contain `...` to pass on other arguments. Consequently, the output of the functions does not contain an attribute `package` with the list item `package$path`. This last list item is required for uploading:


```r
source_files <- list.files("R", pattern = ".R$", full.names = TRUE)
test_files <- list.files("inst/tinytest", full.names = TRUE)
cov <- covr::file_coverage(source_files = source_files, test_files = test_files)
covr::codecov(coverage = cov, quiet = FALSE)
#> Error in if (file.exists(path_to_yaml)) { : argument is of length zero
```


I think that the error is derived from the `extract_from_yaml()` function in this line when `token` is not set (in my case, it's the environmental variable `CODECOV_TOKEN`):

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/c6d10d9b6ffec0521e49eb5388f5e3a6d47e4bd7/R/codecov.R#L197

The hack is quite straightforward though:

```r
attr(cov, which = "package") <- list(path = ".")
covr::codecov(coverage = cov, quiet = FALSE)
#> $message
#> [1] "Coverage reports upload successfully"
#> 
#> $uploaded
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> (...)
```

So I reckon the `file_coverage()` or the `extract_from_yaml()` function requires a small fix 🙂

title: test for missing packages fails
description:
My package implements some S3 methods for classes which are defined by packages in Suggests.  Before using those packages in the methods, I check for the presence of the relevant packages using `requireNamespace()`, and throw an error if it's not present.  But this is a difficult error to test!  I have something like this:

```r
requireBiostrings <- function() {
  if (!requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly = TRUE) {
    stop("Package 'Biostrings' is required for operating on 'XStringSet' objects")
  }
}
```

Then, in test_require.R:
```r
# Everything in "Suggests" is automatically loaded for testing, so it must be unloaded first.
# In practice other loaded packages which import Biostrings
# have to be unloaded before Biostrings, but they are omitted for brevity
unloadNamespace("Biostrings")
test_that("requireBiostrings raises error without Biostrings",
  # run with an empty library path so Biostrings can't be found
  withr::with_temp_libpaths(
    {
      expect_false("Biostrings" %in% loadedNamespaces())
      expect_error(requireBiostrings(), "Package 'Biostrings' is required for operating on 'XStringSet' objects")
    },
    action = "replace"
  )
)
```

This works during `devtools::test()`, but the `expect_error()` fails during `covr::package_coverage()`.  I know I can just use `function_exclusions` to skip these functions when calculating coverage, but is there any way to actually test them in `covr`?

title: environment_coverage fails if line_exclusions = NULL
description:
I was writing a simple toy example for `environment_coverage()`, but if the parameter `line_exclusions` is left as NULL (the default), I get an error.

```r
my_env <-  new.env()
my_env$add <- function(x, y) { x + y }
cat("add(1, 2) == 3", file="add_test.R")
environment_coverage(my_env, test_files = "add_test.R")
```
`Error: Full file exclusions must be character vectors of length 1. items: 1 are not!`

Not sure if I'm using it correctly, but on further investigation, I think this function is only really ever used by `devtools::test_coverage_file()` which seems to work fine without line/file exclusions, so I'll just exclude it from the list of functions in my documentation PR as the toy example I'm using is a bit overly simplistic anyway.

title: Updating Codecov script to mirror bash script
description:
Hi, Tom from Codecov here. I noticed an uptick in our `R` code coverage, and I wanted to introduce myself and see what I can do to help. I am not an `R` developer nor am I too familiar with the ecosystem, so you'll have to forgive me for any mistakes. 

Looking at the code, I notice two improvements that could be made
1. uploading using the v4 endpoint as opposed to v2 and
2. adding more CI/CDs to CI detection. I am happy to write a PR if that is helpful.

Although we do offer other community uploaders like our [Ruby uploader](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-ruby), we have been trying to move towards wrappers on top of our [bash uploader](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-bash) like our [Action](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action) to ensure the latest and greatest. Would this be interesting to you at all?

title: devtools::test() and R CMD check ok but covr throws error
description:
My package lagged' passes `devtools::test()`, `R CMD check`, and builds successfully on TravisCI. However for some reason Coveralls was not getting coverage updates from Travis. It turned out that it was the 'covr' run after the build that was failing in the following line at the end of my `.travis.yml`
```
after_success:
  - Rscript -e 'covr::coveralls()'
```
More specifically, running the coverage tests locally I got:
```
library("covr")
package_coverage()
## ── 1. Failure: slMatrix (@test-pc20slMatrix.r#64)  ──────────────
## `nSeasons(msl) <- 5` threw an error with unexpected message.
## Expected match: "unable to find an inherited method for function 'nSeasons<-'"
## Actual message: "unable to find an inherited method for function ‘nSeasons<-’ for signature 
## ‘\"slMatrix\"’"
```
It is the quotes that cause the problem, but surprisingly for me, changing the quotes to dots in the  expected regex didn't work:
```
── 1. Failure: slMatrix (@test-pc20slMatrix.r#64)  ────────
`nSeasons(msl) <- 5` threw an error with unexpected message.
Expected match: "unable to find an inherited method for function .nSeasons<-."
Actual message: "unable to find an inherited method for function ‘nSeasons<-’ for signature ‘\"slMatrix\"’"
```
It looks like there is a discrepancy between 'covr' and devtools here. I know that the above is not a 'minimal' reprex but it seems to convey the issue. The offending line above, now commented out  is at the end of the file  (see `GeoBosh/lagged`).

I resolved the issue by cutting off the regex just before the first quote but the expectation becomes less expressive this way.

title: Feature Request: Recording srcrefs of test expressions & link to covr traces
description:
It would be super helpful if, in addition to the srcrefs of the code that gets executed by each test, we could also record the srcrefs of the unit tests that trigger their evaluation.

# Motivation

I'm helping to develop an R package validation strategy, and one feature that would be tremendously valuable would be the ability to link individual unit tests to the traces that execute during the test execution. By linking the annotated test behavior to the trace that is executed, we can automate the construction of a traceability matrix, an expected part of any validation report. 

# Work so far

I've built up a proof of concept in a fork at [dgkf/covr@dev/testrefs](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/tree/dev/testrefs). However, to keep changes minimal, I've recorded a list of srcrefs (called `testrefs`) associated with the test for each and every trace (so that the length of `$testrefs` will be equal to `$value`).

```r
covr_result <- covr::package_coverage("./example")
covr_result[[1]]
# $value 
# [1] 1
#
# $srcref
# return("example result")
#
# $functions
# [1] "example"
#
# $testrefs
# $testrefs[[1]]
# test_that("example function communicates wip structure.", {
#   expect_silent(example())
# })
```

In my benchmarks, I found that execution time is minimally affected (~5% overhead). However, one big limitation of this approach is how much redundant information is recorded. Each and every call in the stack is recording a copy of the test trace. This results in quite large coverage objects (~50-100x tmp file size, and coverage object.size). There are certainly ways of collecting this data more thoughtfully, but it would affect more of the covr codebase.

# Proposed Changes to `coverage` Data Structure

If there's interest in including this additional data, I would propose a data structure that

1. Keeps existing data in the same place to minimize impact to existing `covr` code
2. Adds a list of test srcrefs as an attribute to the `coverage` object (`attr(,"tests")`)
3. Add a `tests` matrix  to each item within the `coverage` object list, which has a row per execution of the trace and columns for test number (corresponding to index in the test srcrefs attributes) and stack depth into the target package during execution (allowing differentiation of calls directly from the test from those that are called from within the package). 

```r
> unclass(covr_result)
# $example.R:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8
# $`example.R:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8`$value
# [1]  1
# $`example.R:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8`$srcref
# return("example result")
#
# $`example.R:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8`$functions
# [1] "example"
#
# $`example.R:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8`$tests
#       test depth
# [1,]     1     1
#
# attr(,"tests")  # list of test expression srcrefs
# [[1]]
# test_that("example function communicates wip structure.", {
#   expect_silent(example())
# })
#
# attr(,"package")  # other attributes already part of coverage objects
# ...
#
# attr(,"relative")
# ...
```

I'm happy to help implement the changes, but wanted to gauge interest in adding this functionality before making changes that might affect more of the codebase.

description:
Hi there,
first of all thanks for this cool package that I use in my azure build pipelines all the time.
Since upgrading testthat to the 3rd edition and making use of the newly introduced test fixtures with a project scope (tests/testthat/setup.R) my builds started to fail. By looking at the way tests are performed inside the covr package, I realised that covr uses the tools::testInstalledPackage function to perform package tests, which tests each test file in an individual R process and does not know about any package wide fixtures introduced in a setup file.
If you know about this incompability, are there any plans to resolve this?
Thanks,
Janis

title: `parse_gcov` assumes that produced source file names are escaped regular expressions
description:
The function `parse_gcov` tries to skip all files for which `source_file` is not below root `package_path`. It does that by using a regular expression. 

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/ebf0e7fc215ef91aeeb43ffcbe945e116e6e0187/R/compiled.R#L14

However, `rex::regex` assumes that the given expression is already an escaped regular expression. That might not be always the case - MacOS is allowing almost all Unicode characters in filenames. In my case, a parent folder contains a "+" (that, unfortunately, cannot be changed). 

The effects might vary, but I guess in most cases, the files are simply ignored such that no reports on compiled files are returned.

It should be able to solve this by replacing the relevant expression with 

```r
grepl(rex::rex(start, rex::regex(paste0(rex::escape(package_path), collapse = "|"))), source_file)
```

Possible link to #448.

I ran `package_coverage(quiet = FALSE, clean = FALSE)` and looked at the log, but essentially the line that fails is `test_check("collapse")`, which can also be seen on Travis-CI (https://travis-ci.com/github/SebKrantz/collapse) where is says a segmentation fault was encountered. Reading through the covr website, this could be perhaps because it was not possible to properly restart the R session before running the tests. I also noticed that running `devtools::test()` was problematic after the altered compilation with the `-O0 --coverage` flags: Sometimes the package fails to load, so the testing cannot start, and sometimes they run but all tests involving compiled code fail. Possibly the compilation itself is therefore problematic. I noticed that there are still `-O2` and other default flags. This is an example of how one cpp file is compiled through `package_coverage`:

```
"C:/RBuildTools/4.0/mingw64/bin/"g++  -std=gnu++11 -I"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-40~1.2/include" -DNDEBUG  -I'C:/Users/Sebastian Krantz/Documents/R/win-library/4.0/Rcpp/include'        -O2 -Wall  -mfpmath=sse -msse2 -mstackrealign -O0 --coverage -c fNdistinct.cpp -o fNdistinct.o
```

Having encountered these difficulties which I am not sure how to solve, I wanted to turn off coverage of all compiled code until I found a solution (which might be difficult since almost all of my functions call compiled code). I also failed to do that. My approaches were: 

`cov <- package_coverage(quiet = FALSE, line_exclusions = as.list(paste0("src/", list.files("src"))))`
This did not work, files were still compiled. Then I included a `.covignore` file in the root directory with the lines

```
src
/src/
*.cpp
*.c
```
which also yielded no response. Finally I tried to set `options(covr.exclude_pattern = ".cpp")` (which is probably not the intended use but anyway) - without success. 

It would be great if you could let me know how to either get this running for all of my code or how to exclude my compiled code from the coverage testing. - presumably I'm not the only one with such issues. 

Thanks,

Sebastian

title: Using covr in combination with withr::with_options may lead to problems
description:
`covr` sets some options in `.onLoad` to default values. This can lead to problems when the package is loaded inside a `withr::with_options` call. E.g.
```r
# covr not loaded yet
withr::with_options(list("covr.exclude_start" = "#^"),  # disable exclude regions
  covr::file_coverage("<some R file>", "test.R")
)
```
No problems! However, `with_options` resets the `"covr.exclude_start"` option to `NULL` afterwards, so the following fails:
```r
covr::file_coverage("<some R file>", "test.R")
#> Error in regexpr(pattern = pattern, data, perl = TRUE, ...) : 
#>   invalid 'pattern' argument
```
(The workaround so far is obviously "load `covr` before `with_options`" or `unloadNamespace("covr")` afterwards)

title: covr and devtools::test disagree on some function objects equivalence
description:
I know that equality of objects containing environments is a matter of definition but report this since under `covr` I obtained different results for some tests compared to just running `devtools::test() or `R CMD check`. 

It is difficult for me to devise a reprex. The following is an excerpt from one of the last lines, now commented, of [test-exampleModels.R](https://github.com/GeoBosh/mixAR/blob/master/tests/testthat/test-exampleModels.R). In essence the problem arises when comparing two function components of the compared objects. The following comparison succeeds in `devtools::test()` (also under `R CMD check`) 
```
expect_equal(moT_B, exampleModels$WL_Bt_1)
```
but `covr::report()` (also on TravisCI) throws error and reports that
```
## Attributes: < Component "dist": Component "generator":
##        target, current do not match when deparsed
```
Those objects look the same:
```
moT_B@dist$generator
## function(par = numeric(0)){
##                 dist <- ed_skeleton(par, fixed = fixed, n = length(type), tr = tr)
##                 for(i in seq_along(type)){
##                     dist[[i]] <- dist[[i]](ed_src[[ type[i] ]])
##                 }
##                 dist
##             }
## <environment: 0x55a7fea7e9c0>

exampleModels$WL_Bt_1@dist$generator
## function(par = numeric(0)){
##                 dist <- ed_skeleton(par, fixed = fixed, n = length(type), tr = tr)
##                 for(i in seq_along(type)){
##                     dist[[i]] <- dist[[i]](ed_src[[ type[i] ]])
##                 }
##                 dist
##             }
## <environment: 0x55a7ff72b258>
```
apart from the environments of course. Their environments are `expect_equal`:
```
expect_equal(environment(exampleModels$WL_Bt_1@dist$generator),
                       environment(moT_B@dist$generator))
```
The enclosing environments in both cases are the package environments:
```
parent.env(environment(moT_B@dist$generator))
## <environment: namespace:mixAR>
parent.env(environment(exampleModels$WL_Bt_1@dist$generator))
## <environment: namespace:mixAR>
```
Could it be that under `covr` the comparison doesn't stop when hitting the namespace of the package?

title: Testing function equality in a covr-compatible way?
description:
Consider an R package with just 1 source file, say `hello.R` with the following content:

```r
hello <- function() "hi"
ciao <- function() "hi"
```

And a test file (e.g. using testthat it can look as follows):

```r
test_that(
  "Functions are identical",
  expect_identical(hello, ciao)
)
```

This test will pass running it with different methods (`tools::testInstalledPackage()` included).

However trying to compute the coverage using `covr::package_coverage(...)`, it will cause an error. Investigating by putting `dput(hello); dput(ciao)` in the test script, we can see from running `covr::package_coverage(...)`:

```
`hello` not identical to `ciao`.
target, current do not match when deparsed

function () 
{
    covr:::count("hello.R:1:10:1:24:10:24:3:3")
    "hi"
}
function () 
{
    covr:::count("hello.R:2:9:2:23:9:23:4:4")
    "hi"
}
```

So essentially is seems `covr` has put code inside the function bodies that makes them non-identical. Are there any best practices on how to prevent these issues when comparing functions as part of testing?

Thanks!

Some `sessionInfo()`:
- Using covr_3.5.0, R version 3.4.4 (2018-03-15), Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit), Running under: Ubuntu 18.04.1 LTS

title: file_coverage should trace code run using parallel::mc*
description:
I currently use this slightly adapted version of `file_coverage` to also trace code run using `mclapply`, `mcparallel`, etc.:
```
file_coverage <- function(source_files, test_files, line_exclusions = NULL,
                          function_exclusions = NULL, parent_env = parent.frame()) {
  tdir <- tempfile("covr_traces_")
  dir.create(tdir)
  fix_mcexit(paste0("'", tdir, "'"))

  env <- new.env(parent = parent_env)
  withr::with_options(c(keep.parse.data.pkgs = TRUE), {
    lapply(source_files, sys.source, keep.source = TRUE,
           envir = env)
  })
  trace_environment(env)
  on.exit({
    reset_traces()
    clear_counters()
  })
  lapply(test_files, sys.source, keep.source = TRUE, envir = env)

  save_trace(tdir)
  coverage <- structure(merge_coverage(list.files(tdir, full.names = TRUE)),
                        class = "coverage")
  exclude(coverage, line_exclusions = line_exclusions, function_exclusions = function_exclusions,
          path = NULL)
}
```
Maybe you want to consider adding this to covr? I guess, one would certainly want to make patching `parallel:::mcexit` optional, just as it is for `package_coverage`.

title: What should one do when tests take too much time
description:
Hi all. This is more a of a question about best practices than a code issue. My team and I develop the [geobr](https://github.com/ipeaGIT/geobr) package to download geospatial data sets of Brazil. We have written some tests covering almost 70% of the package. The problem is that it there are too many tests and it takes lot of time to run all of them, so the package fails on **CRAN** submission and on **Travis** tests.

I've been using the arguments `skip_on_cran()` and `skip_on_travis()` but then **Codecov** does not capture correct  the coverage level of the package. Is there a best practice / recommendation on how one should deal with this ? 

ps. Thanks for your help in advance and congrats for developing such a great package!
