title: Coverage not counted on brace lines
description:
I think that this is subtly different than #363, but it is related.  (Sorry if it is a duplicate.)

When I have a function factory similar to #363 (see https://codecov.io/gh/billdenney/pknca/commit/cef59c91c5ac4ecc39ed5a73b4f784844d0bc1fb#D7-255, specifically lines 255, 258, and 260), the interstitial parts of if blocks are not counted: the closing braces and the else.

I see from #363 that 251 and 261 are not run during testing, so they need a `#nocov`, and I know that I could add `#nocov` to lines 255, 258, and 260, but if it's reasonable to have covr detect that those lines are implicitly tested, that seems preferable.

title: Traceability matrices.
Add warning if tests do not use argument values other than the defaults
description:
Hello!

As a Carpentries instructor, I'm considering to include a section about code/test coverage in a lesson for intermediate R users. I noticed that `covr` does not penalise tests which reuse a function's default argument values, rather than sending their own. I presume that this is intended, and that a dedicated [argument/parameter value coverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_coverage#Parameter_value_coverage) may be a bit out-of-scope.

However, might `covr` users benefit from it checking whether any non-default values for function arguments with a default are used in the tests, and if so, showing a warning (or message)?

I imagine that this could help unit-testing-novices to understand that other coverages besides `if` & `else` branches can be important.

What do you think?

cc @cbeleites for suggesting `covr::report()` to me which got me thinking about this.

> Edit: Hadn't finished drafting when I accidentally hit `Submit`...

title: Skip inserting covr::count() on specified lines
percent_coverage is broken or inadequately documented
description:
Following up on #374 and [my call for community help](https://community.rstudio.com/t/return-overall-percentage-of-coverage-from-covr-codecov/33588), I did a bit more research. On my local machine, I ran:

```
library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("jpritikin/covr")  # based on 1.2.0-520-ge344676
library(covr)
library(roxygen2)
library(withr)

options(covr.gcov = "gcov-9")

withr::with_envvar(c(MAKE="make -j4"), {
  withr::with_makevars(getOption("covr.flags"), assignment = "+=", {
    utils::install.packages(
      ".", repos = NULL, type = "source",
      INSTALL_opts = c("--example",  "--install-tests", "--with-keep.source",
                       "--with-keep.parse.data", "--no-multiarch")
    )
  })
})
roxygenize('.', roclets=c('rd'))
c1 <- covr::package_coverage(type=c("tests","examples"), quiet=TRUE, pre_clean=FALSE)
pl <- covr:::per_line(c1)
s1 <- (t(sapply(pl, function(x) c(total=length(x$coverage),
                                 possible=sum(!is.na(x$coverage)),
                                 covered=sum(!is.na(x$coverage) & x$coverage > 0)))))
s1 <- as.data.frame(s1)
s1$pending = s1$possible - s1$covered
t1 <- colSums(s1[,2:4])
t1['covered'] / t1['possible']
```

title: Curly braces added by covr can lead to problems with rlang's curly curly interpolation

title: Add support for specifying `CODECOV_TOKEN` in .yml file
description:
Token for upload to codecov.io can be specified both with env var (`CODECOV_TOKEN`) and with .yml file by adding following into `codecov.yml`:
```
codecov:
  token: token
```
Specifying it in `.yml` file allows to set it independently in situations when one doesn't have access to environment where actual coverage report will be run (e.g., in staging/production).

title: Could output of package_coverage show the end of the failed file rather than beginning?
description:
Running `package_coverage` (via `coveralls`) is hitting an error in my tests. But the output from `package_coverage` only shows the top of the file with the error, which only shows information about loading the package, so that I can't see what the error is. It would be helpful if it instead showed the end of the file, where the error report would be. This would be particularly helpful on travisCI where I can't dig up the temporary file.

For example (from my `clusterExperiment` package on TravisCI) [](https://travis-ci.org/epurdom/clusterExperiment/builds/383108569#L1469):

title: skipping lines in a test
Coverage of functions not found by trace_environment
description:
I am trying to get `covr` to run with a package that uses constructs of the form
```R
wrapFunction <- function(infun) {
  function(...) {
    infun(...)
  }
}

isNotCovered <- wrapFunction(function(p1, p2) {
  p3 <- p1 + p2
  p3
})
```
with the tests calling `isNotCovered(...)`.

When running `package_coverage` naively, `covr` does not find the two last lines of code, since they are hidden in the `environment` of what ends up being `isNotCovered()`. In fact, the generated shiny page looks like this:
![coverage](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15801081/33900579-3af707f2-df6f-11e7-8e6a-fe0bd50fbdbd.png)

Is there any way to announce to `covr` the presence of this function? I've tried add run things like
```R
covr:::replace(covr:::replacement("infun", environment()))
```
and
```R
infun = covr:::trace_calls(infun)
```
inside `wrapFunction` *and* inside the anonymous function within `wrapFunction`, but when I then run `package_coverage` I always get the error

```R
> covx = covr::package_coverage("dummy")
Error: identical(names(y), names) is not TRUE
Enter a frame number, or 0 to exit

1: covr::package_coverage("dummy")
2: merge_coverage(trace_files)
3: stopifnot(identical(names(y), names))
```
When inspecting this, it seems like the srcrefs in both trace files are incompatible?

Is there a way to either make `package_coverage` find functions hidden in environments automatically, or to cause them to be traced manually?

title: Enable parse data when installing packages for R devel
description:
R-devel will disable use of parse data by default, so we will need to explicitly enable it in those versions. This patch from @kalibera is what is needed in R-devel, although we will need to use something like `option("keep.parse.data.pkgs" = TRUE)` and `Sys.setenv( R_KEEP_PKG_PARSE_DATA="yes")` so we can maintain backwards compatibility.

```diff
diff -ru orig/covr/R/covr.R covr/R/covr.R
--- orig/covr/R/covr.R  2017-08-15 06:53:59.000000000 -0500
+++ covr/R/covr.R       2018-04-24 03:23:47.758433338 -0500
@@ -85,7 +85,7 @@
   env <- new.env(parent = parent_env)

   lapply(source_files,
-     sys.source, keep.source = TRUE, envir = env)
+     sys.source, keep.source = TRUE, keep.parse.data = TRUE, envir = env)

   trace_environment(env)
   on.exit({
@@ -94,7 +94,7 @@
   })

   lapply(test_files,
-     sys.source, keep.source = TRUE, envir = env)
+     sys.source, keep.source = TRUE, keep.parse.data = TRUE, envir = env)

   coverage <- structure(as.list(.counters), class = "coverage")

@@ -257,6 +257,7 @@
                             INSTALL_opts = c("--example",
                                              "--install-tests",
"--with-keep.source",
+ "--with-keep.parse.data",
                                              "--no-multiarch"),
                             quiet = quiet))
```

title: path error with covr but not with testthat or R CMD Check
description:
I came accross a very strange example, in which testthat works but codecov does not. I tried to minimalize the example as much as possible and created a package `reprexpkg` that contains just one test that works with testthat but not with codecov.
Essentially, the following test in is the problem

```r
test_that("test with tempdir", {
  dir <- tempfile("styler")
  dir.create(dir)
  path_temp <- file.path(dir, "repeated_parsing-in.R")
  path_perm <- rprojroot::find_testthat_root_file("repeated_parsing-in.R")
  file.copy(path_perm, dir)
  path_out <- gsub("\\-.*$", "\\-in\\.R", path_perm)
  identical(path_out, path_perm)
  #> TRUE
  ref <- enc::read_lines_enc(path_perm) # does not work with path_out, only works with path_term
  unlink(dir)
})
```
As soon as you replace `path_perm` with `path_out` (which ought to be identical), calling `covr::package_coverage()` won't work anymore but `devtools::test()` still does.

Any ideas why that happens and how one could fix it? Any help would be appreciated, although we found a workaround already. You can clone the package from here to reproduce the error (however, I can understand it if it's too much of work): https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/reprexpkg

title: Code coverage calculation hangs when executing parallel code on Travis CI
description:
I am experiencing an issue in calculating the code coverage for our Bioconductor package PharmacoGx. It is very similar to one I had with executing testthat when trying to calculate test coverage, but the workaround which succeeded for testthat does not seem to help with running codecov. The test that issue is below:
https://github.com/hadley/testthat/issues/602

The issue specifically is that when running `codecov` interactively on my machine,  it runs fine in about 15 minutes and outputs results. However, when run on Travis CI, the code hangs for over an hour, and does not produce output. I have narrowed the appearance of the issue down to adding this test:
```
library(PharmacoGx)
require(parallel)
context("Checking intersectPSet.")
test_that("Intersection result did not change since last time", {
	data(GDSCsmall)
	data(CCLEsmall)
	expect_equal_to_reference(intersectPSet(list('GDSC'=GDSCsmall, 'CCLE'=CCLEsmall), intersectOn = c("drugs", "cell.lines","concentrations")), "intersectedSmallData.rds")
})
```

The function `intersectPSet` contains a call to `makeCluster` and `parSapply`. In the case of testthat, the issue was that R CMD check was setting a environmental variable `Sys.setenv(R_TESTS="startup.Rs")`, using a relative path, and the file startup.Rs did not exist in the tests/testthat directory. I believe the parallel workers spawned with that as their working directory, causing the issue. Two workarounds proposed were to create this file as empty in the right directory, or to add `Sys.unsetenv("R_TESTS")` to the beginning of the `testthat.R` script. I have applied both in hopes one of the two would help with the issue of `codecov` hanging, but neither seems to have any effect. I suspect this has to do with how codecov sets up the environment where it does its tests when running on Travis CI.

(The issue was discussed on R PKG devel mailing list: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2017q1/001316.html)

Could someone with more knowledge of the covr package take a look? It would be great if I could reproduce the hanging on my own machine but it seems to only happen on Travis, making debugging tricky.

title: Functions wrapped in `covr:::count()`: an edge case
description:

In the middle of the graph below, I was hovering over `reg1()` (near the middle), which revealed that the function body of `reg1()` was wrapped in a call to `covr:::count()`. Is there anything I can do to prevent some functions from being wrapped? Maybe with a protected environment?

title: package_coverage fails if testthat::test_path is used in test files
description:
This came up over at https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/114 :

Because `testInstalledPackage` runs tests in a _pkg_-tests subdirectory any usage of the `test_path` function from `testthat` within test files causes the error

```
Error: Can't find `tests/testthat/` in current directory.
```

when `package_coverage` is run. Removing the usage of `test_path` gets rid of the problem.

Unless I've missed it somewhere (in which case sorry!), this isn't documented. `test_path` is probably used widely enough that a warning about this could be a good addition to the documentation.

title: covr fails because testthat fails because lintr fails because it ignores `.lintr`
description:
Hi @jimhester,

I am not 100% if this is a `covr` or `lintr` issue but I have the following problem:

I run `testthat` test including linting with `lintr` to ensure proper style.
There are a few linters I don't want to run (as I break their style suggestions willingly).
Those, I disable through a `.lintr` file.
Without `covr` this works just fine (thus this `covr` issue).

If, for the same repository, I add `covr` (without linting), it works, too (thus maybe a `lintr` issue)?

However, if I enable both `covr` & `lintr`, `testthat` tests run successfully (incl. linting, but ignoring the linters specified in `.lintr`), but `covr` fails *and* @lintr-bot complains about the *disabled* linters.

I tracked this down to `coveralls()` running the tests (incl. linting) which fail, as `lintr` complains about breaking the *disabled* linters.

I'm working on a minimal working example to better demonstrate the issue, but maybe this is already enough to help me.

Best,
Marcel

title: Testing, and function exclusions, fail with weirdly created functions
description:
Here's a test case for a small package:

```
#' A foo
#'
#' With some foo
#'
#' @export
foo <- function(x, ...) UseMethod('foo')

make_foo_hux <- function() {
  assign('foo.huxtable', eval(bquote(function(x, ...) "hi")), envir = parent.frame() )
}

#' @rdname foo
#' @name foo.huxtable
#' @method foo huxtable
#' @export
NULL

make_foo_hux()
```

A complete source directory for the package is attached:

[packagefileprob.tar.gz](https://github.com/jimhester/covr/files/864373/packagefileprob.tar.gz)

When I run `package_coverage()` in the base directory, I get 

> Error in vapply(x, function(x) getSrcFilename(x$srcref, full.names = TRUE),  : 
>   values must be length 1,
>  but FUN(X[[2]]) result is length 0
> 

OK, fair enough, I'm doing something weird to create that function, it's not surprising that covr struggles with it. But when I run `package_coverage(function_exclusions = 'foo')` I get the same error. The traceback leads to `filter_non_package_files`.

title: Change of covr license to GPL-3
description:
covr is currently MIT licensed, however a strict reading of the GPL-2 license for
dependency [withr](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/withr/index.html)
(which is GPL >= 2) would require covr to also be GPL-2 or GPL-3. Oracle's'
legal representation suggested `LICENSE MIT + file LICENSE + Portions GPLv3 with Additional Permission |
GPLv3`, but as this is a non-standard license it will be flagged by CRAN and
create additional maintenance hassles going forward.

Because of these concerns I now feel the most expedient thing to do is to
change the covr license to GPL-3, however in order to do so I will need
approval from all contributors (listed below). Please reply to this issue with
either
 - I accept the change of covr license to GPL-3
 - I reject the change of covr license to GPL-3

We can only change license if we get acceptance from all contributors.

title: Incomplete gcov parsing
description:
Related to #164, but I think it's better to open a new issue, since it seems to be a parsing issue at the end. I run `package_coverage(clean = F)` and the `.gcov` output for [this file](https://coveralls.io/builds/7731688/source?filename=src%2Fentity.h) is the following:

```
        -:    0:Source:entity.h
        -:    0:Graph:/home/.../simmer/src/simmer_rcpp.gcno
        -:    0:Data:/home/.../simmer/src/simmer_rcpp.gcda
        -:    0:Runs:3
        -:    0:Programs:1
        -:    1:#ifndef ENTITY_H
        -:    2:#define ENTITY_H
        -:    3:
        -:    4:#include "simmer.h"
        -:    5:
        -:    6:#define SUCCESS 0
        -:    7:#define ENQUEUED -1
        -:    8:#define REJECTED -2
        -:    9:
        -:   10:// forward declarations
        -:   11:class Simulator;
        -:   12:
        -:   13:/** 
        -:   14: *  Base class. Every element in a simulation model is an entity.
        -:   15: */
    #####:   16:class Entity {
        -:   17:public:
    #####:   18:  CLONEABLE(Entity)
        -:   19:  
        -:   20:  Simulator* sim;
        -:   21:  std::string name;
        -:   22:  
    #####:   23:  Entity(Simulator* sim, std::string name, int mon)
    #####:   24:    : sim(sim), name(name), mon(std::abs(mon)) {}
    #####:   25:  virtual ~Entity() {}
    #####:   26:  virtual void reset() {};
    #####:   27:  int is_monitored() { return mon; }
        -:   28:  
        -:   29:private:
        -:   30:  int mon;
        -:   31:};
        -:   32:
        -:   33:#endif
```

Ok, no coverage, as shown in Coveralls. The issue comes out when you parse all these `gcov` files (`.gcov`, `.gcda`, `.gcno`) with `lcov`. The output of `lcov` is the following:

```
       1             : #ifndef ENTITY_H
       2             : #define ENTITY_H
       3             : 
       4             : #include "simmer.h"
       5             : 
       6             : #define SUCCESS 0
       7             : #define ENQUEUED -1
       8             : #define REJECTED -2
       9             : 
      10             : // forward declarations
      11             : class Simulator;
      12             : 
      13             : /** 
      14             :  *  Base class. Every element in a simulation model is an entity.
      15             :  */
      16          16 : class Entity {
      17             : public:
      18           0 :   CLONEABLE(Entity)
      19             :   
      20             :   Simulator* sim;
      21             :   std::string name;
      22             :   
      23        4126 :   Entity(Simulator* sim, std::string name, int mon)
      24        4126 :     : sim(sim), name(name), mon(std::abs(mon)) {}
      25        2861 :   virtual ~Entity() {}
      26           0 :   virtual void reset() {};
      27       11555 :   int is_monitored() { return mon; }
      28             :   
      29             : private:
      30             :   int mon;
      31             : };

      33             : #endif
```

Magic! :D From which I understand that `.gcov` files don't tell the whole story. Apparently, there is more info about those lines marked with `#####` in the `.gcda` and `.gcno` files (which are in binary format, BTW) that must be taken into account.

title: automatic detection of parallel support
description:
Just had the case: if a package does not use parallel::mcparallel directly, but indirectly from another package, the uses_parallel() function will fail to detect it, and package_coverage will fail (with the usual error from https://github.com/jimhester/covr/blob/master/R/covr.R#L276). 

By the way, merge_coverage() should fail with a more informative message.
Or it could accept truncated traces, and just merge them.

title: report depends on temporary files
description:
Hi,
When a html report is generated using report(cov, "foo.html"), this foo.html references temporary files, that will be deleted when the R process which generated the report exits.

So you can not view the report after, and you must have an interactive session. 
It could be nice to have an option (e.g. dir=tempfile()) to specify where to save these files.

title: `R CMD check --run-dontcheck` -- equivalent for covr
description:
Not urgent, but would nice:  If you have `\dontcheck{...}` sections in your help examples, typically because checking takes too much time,  recent versions of  `R CMD check` remind you to run  regularly / occasionally

It would valuable to be able to also measure coverage when these additional examples are run.

title: Coverage for "dynamically" Generated Functions
description:
This one is pretty low priority since it is a fairly esoteric corner case:

```
make_fun_1 <- function() {
  function(x) {
    1 + 1
    2 + 2
    cat("fun1\n")
  }
}
fun1 <- make_fun_1()
```

With a test file that calls `fun1()`  does not show coverage of `1 + 1`, etc. even though that code is run.  I suspect this is different to issue #113 since `fun1` should be detected as a function in the namespace.  Likely the problem is that the function definition itself doesn't exist in a concrete manner that can be systematically defined in the source code.

I'm guessing the most likely outcome for this issue is "wontfix", but posting here just in case there is actually a simple resolution.

In case you're wondering about why anyone would ever want to do this: I happen to have a family of functions that are all almost the same and share the same formal arguments, so rather than defining each function separately I use a constructing function to avoid having to re-state a lengthy argument list every time (and risk messing it up for one of the functions when tweaking, etc.).

title: using mcparallel with coverage
description:
I modified a TestPackage from covr, replacing the test by:

```
test_that("test_me works", {
  library(parallel)
  mccollect(mcparallel(
    expect_equal(test_me(2, 2), 4)
  ))
})
```

when doing this, the code is not covered. Obviously commenting out the mcparallel makes the coverage work again. 
It seems that the **reg.finalizer()** handler is not called when the process forked by mcparallel() terminates.
You can see that by running this script:

```
load_and_hook_cover <- function() {
  library(covr)
  ns <- .getNamespace('covr')
  reg.finalizer(ns, function(...) { cat('finalizing covr\n') }, onexit = TRUE)
}
library(parallel)
res <- mccollect(mcparallel({load_and_hook_cover(); gc()}, silent = FALSE))
```

I think it is due to parallel:::mcexit, because this seems to work:

```
load_and_hook_cover <- function() {
  library(covr)
  ns <- .getNamespace('covr')
  reg.finalizer(ns, function(...) { cat('finalizing covr\n') }, onexit = TRUE)
}
library(parallel)

fixed_mcexit <- function(...) { cat('faking mcexit\n'); quit('no')}
assignInNamespace('mcexit', fixed_mcexit, .getNamespace('parallel'))

res <- mccollect(mcparallel({load_and_hook_cover(); gc()}, silent = FALSE))
```

title: is on.exit(clear_counters()) needed in package_coverage() ?
description:
About this line:
cf https://github.com/jimhester/covr/blob/master/R/covr.R#L174

From what I understood, the package code is traced in another process, so the counters of the current namespace in the current process should not be modified, hence my question...

The reason I'm asking is in the case of recursive package_coverage() calls, where some traced code (say of package A), contains a call to package_coverage() to compute the coverage of yet another package (say B). At the end of the package_coverage call executed by the R code in A, the counters will be reset (by the on.exit) so that further code will not only be improperly traced (previous tracing is deleted), but will lead to incomplete trace files.

title: Problem checking coverage in switch statments & work around
description:
In the released and github version of covr I had a problem checking coverage in switch statements. I found a simple work around.

I have a switch that selects based on a string. The different choices are all marked covered even if they are not.

Here is a small example of the code:

``` R
switch(slot,
    modelname = name.lp(lprec, name=value),
    modelsense = lp.control(lprec, sense=value),
    obj = set.objfn(lprec, rep_len(value, ncol)),
    lb = set.bounds(lprec, lower = rep_len(value, ncol))
    )
```

I am only testing one of the slots values but all are marked as covered.

The work around that solved the problem for me was to surround each switch selection with { }'s, e.g.

`modelname   = { name.lp(lprec, name=value)},`

This solved the problem and gave me correct coverage numbers.

A crude solution would be to parse the `.Rd` files under `man` and put their contents into one file that would be run as a test.

title: WISH: Add option/argument to run through all tests although some give errors
description:
I'd like to suggest to add an option/argument so that covr keeps running through all tests instead of stopping whenever a test fails.  Something like `run_tests(..., on_error="warn")`.

Why?  I once in a while find that covr gives errors when `R CMD check` doesn't.  If it occurs on my local machine, I can often either troubleshoot and find a fix, or simple skip the test when `covr` is loaded.  However, when I cannot reproduce the problem locally and it appears on, say, Travis CI, it is complicated and tedious to troubleshoot via trial and error commit/pushing.  Having an option to have covr run through all tests would help, because then you could see what other tests pass/fail, which helps out rule things and narrow in on the troubleshooting.  See for instance https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/future/jobs/101287469#L2564-L2567 (where the covr tests just stops which I assume is due to a test error).

title: src/*.h not covered
description:
# Issue

The covr package reports on the coverage for `R/*.R` and `src/*.c` files, but not `src/*.h`.  Is this something that could easily be fixed?
# Background

We use lots of C macros to emulate templates in C.  For instance, we generate highly data-type optimized `foo_int()` and `foo_double()` functions from template `foo_TYPE()`.  We define `foo_TYPE()` in `src/foo_TYPE.h` whereas the actual functions are defined in `src/foo.c`.  Example:  https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/matrixStats/tree/master/src and https://coveralls.io/builds/3116011

It could be argued whether we should use `src/*.h` the way we do, or if we should move things over to other `src/*.c` files, but if an easy fix, it would be great if covr to cover `src/*.h` files as well.  Also, it may be that covr won't handle macro expansions the way we use them making my request somewhat moot.

title: `quiet` argument to `codecov` not passed on to `package_coverage`
description:
Call to `package_coverage` in `codecov` is [as so](https://github.com/jimhester/covr/blob/master/R/codecov.R#L28):

```
coverage <- package_coverage(...)
```

but perhaps should be

```
coverage <- package_coverage(quiet=quiet,...)
```

since `quiet` is a matched argument for `codecov` already.  Possible work-around is to pass the coverage object already computed:

```
codecov(quiet=FALSE, coverage=package_coverage(quiet=FALSE))
```

title: Document # EXCLUDE COVERAGE START etc?
handling tests skipped by testthat::skip ?
description:
I think `covr` should have the option of not reporting test coverage if any test has been skipped by `testthat::skip`.  

I tend to use the skip function only when a test depends on some external web resource that might not be available.  `testthat:skip` allows intermittent failures to reach that external web resource without the red warning signs of a failed test.  If the tests are being skipped on a particular build because the resource was unavailable, it does not seem reasonable for the coverage to drop instead of just remaining at what it's last value was.  

Not actually sure how to go about this. Would have to dig into @hadley's testthat code to see if `skip` is giving any other programmatic indication that a test has been skipped, other than the visual printing `S` instead of `.` where the test has would have been run in the `testthat` summary.

title: Error: In file(con, "r") : cannot open file '<text>': Invalid argument
description:
If a package uses tools(*) that "dynamically" create functions based on `eval(parse(text=...))` during build, then such functions will have a `srcfile` attribute that is `"<text>"`.  For example:

``` r
> eval(parse(text='foo <- function(...) cat("foo()\n")'))
> attr(attr(foo, "srcref"), "srcfile")
<text>
```

This will cause `covr::coveralls()` to throw an error:

```
> covr::coveralls()
Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(con, "r") : cannot open file '<text>': Invalid argument

6: file(con, "r")
5: FUN(c("<text>")[[1L]], ...)
4: lapply(filenames, readLines)
3: per_line(x)
2: to_coveralls(package_coverage(path, relative_path = TRUE, ...))
1: covr::coveralls()
```

One quick fix is to have `covr::key()` do `gsub("<text>", ".text", ...)` such that they file name, which base on this key, is a valid file name.

Footnotes:
(*) Such tools are `setGenericS3()` and `setMethodS3()` in [R.methodsS3](http://cran.r-project.org/package=R.methodsS3).  Yep, that's my package; I could maybe update those functions to set the `srcfile` attribute such that it points to some kind of source file.  Regardless, there may be other code out there that relies on `eval(parse(text=...))` for creating functions.

title: Changing the default exclusion regexs
description:
@jackwasey, @krlmlr, based on the following github search you are the only people currently using the "EXCLUDE COVERAGE" defaults.

https://github.com/search?p=3&q=language%3Ar+%22EXCLUDE+COVERAGE%22&ref=searchresults&type=Code&utf8=%E2%9C%93

As of ef1f8e0cdb6edbdd94c5959a79b9cd3bea6db412 I am planning on changing these defaults to `# nocov` as the previous defaults were long and kind of obnoxious.

That branch is not merged into trunk yet, but I plan to do so in the near future.

If you want to preserve the previous behavior either pass `exclude="#[[:space:]]*EXCLUDE COVERAGE"` to the call to `package_coverage()` or set `options(covr.exclude = "#[[:space:]]*EXCLUDE COVERAGE")`.  You would have to do the same with the two other exclude search terms as well.

title: set_makevars()/reset_makevars() are not parallel safe
description:
If multiple `covr` sessions are used in parallel (which may not be unlikely on server farms), there is a risk that '~/.R/Makevars' is being rewritten while another R session is reading it leading to a potentially corrupt read.

One way to lower the risk for this is to have `set_makevars()` only modify '~/.R/Makevars' **iff** the content actually changes, i.e. only call `writeLines(..., lines)` if `lines` have changed from the originally read one.  

This solution does not fully cover the case when a pre-existing '~/.R/Makevars' is **changed**, because then `reset_makevars()` in one session will undo what another session might have written.  However, by only rewriting/undoing the file if something changes the risk for incorrect content is lowered.

The long-term solution is probably for R to provide a command-line option/system environment variable where one can specify a session-specific 'Makevars' file path.

title: More robust if set_makevars()/reset_makevars() use file.rename()
description:
If '~/.R/Makevars' exists, then `set_makevars()` rewrites the file and `reset_makevars()` undoes this rewrite.  Although `package_coverage()` uses `on.exit()` to lower the risk for failing to undo the rewrite, there is still a risk that the R session is aborted corrupting the preexisting '~/.R/Makevars' file.  Also, it will mess with the file time stamp in either case.

SUGGESTION:
I would like to propose to have `set_makevars()` to rename any existing file to, say, '~/.R/Makevars.original.covr' and then have `reset_makevars()` to rename it back.  This way the original file is still there in case of a core dump or similar, and its time stamp should be preserved.
